new_jobs.title: Civil/Environmental Engineer
new_jobs.description:
At MacKay, we believe great people are the foundation of our growth and success.

We are in an exciting phase of expansion, creating new opportunities for our employees to take on meaningful work, collaborate across disciplines, and build long-term careers. Whether your role is technical or part of our support services team, you play an important role in delivering high-quality work and helping our projects succeed.

Pioneer Technical Services has built a reputation for delivering innovative engineering and environmental solutions while earning the trust of clients and communities throughout the Intermountain West.

Now, as Pioneer Technical Services, A Part of MacKay, we’re building on that foundation as part of a growing national infrastructure and environmental services firm. Joining MacKay expands opportunities for our employees through multidisciplinary collaboration, broader technical expertise, and the resources of a larger organization, while preserving the collaborative culture, local leadership, and commitment to practical, client-focused solutions that have always defined Pioneer.

We are seeking a Civil/Environmental Engineer
specializing in environmental remediation and heavy-civil earthwork design to join our team at our Kellogg, Idaho
office. The position requires experience across multiple phases of environmental and civil engineering consulting, including preparing technical plans and specifications, managing client and design teams, preparing bidding documents, and overseeing field inspections. The engineer will be required to travel for 10-30% of their time.

Sign-On bonuses available for well-qualified candidates.

Key Responsibilities

Independently perform environmental and civil engineering tasks, including remedial designs for projects within the Silver Valley of Idaho and Western Montana. These designs include conducting alternatives analyses, preparing sampling plans, preparing construction drawings and specifications, preparing bidding documents, and managing construction projects.
Work collaboratively with other engineering disciplines within MacKay, including structural, geotechnical, and water resources engineers.
Conduct technical review and project management for engineering deliverables, schedule, and invoicing.
Manage and mentor junior engineering staff.
Prepare and review technical reports.
Develop scopes of work and budget estimates for conducting engineering projects.
Manage junior staff performing construction observation.
Assist with business development and proposal writing efforts, when warranted.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering or a related discipline
Montana or Idaho P.E. license
5-10 years of experience in Federal and State environmental regulations or related design experience in heavy civil or earth-moving projects.
Proficient in MS Office and AutoCAD Civil 3D
Ability to communicate effectively across all levels and cross-functionally
Ability to collaboratively solve complex technical problems
Experience with proposal development, cost estimating, and determining specifications.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Why Join Pioneer Technical Services – A Part of MacKay?

Pioneer Technical Services is now part of MacKay, a growing national infrastructure and environmental services firm with more than 50 years of experience serving clients across the United States.

While our name will transition to MacKay in January 2027, our people, leadership, and commitment to delivering innovative, practical solutions remain the same. Together, we’re combining Pioneer’s trusted expertise with the expanded resources, multidisciplinary capabilities, and career opportunities of a growing national organization.

At Pioneer, you’ll have the opportunity to work alongside talented professionals on meaningful projects that strengthen communities and the environment. We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, professional development opportunities, and a collaborative culture where employees are empowered to grow and make an impact.

Our Values

At MacKay, our values guide how we work, collaborate, and support one another.

Honesty. We build trust through transparency, integrity, and accountability.
Dedication. We are committed to the success of our team members, clients, and communities.
Relationships. We foster lasting connections that strengthen our work and the teams around us.

Who We Are

MacKay is an infrastructure and environmental services firm built on more than 50 years of experience and a growing collective of expertise.

We are in an exciting phase of growth, expanding our reach, strengthening our capabilities, and bringing together talented teams across the country. That growth is creating new opportunities for our employees to take on meaningful work, collaborate across disciplines, and build long-term careers.

Every role at MacKay contributes to the success of our projects and the clients we serve. Whether your work is technical or operational, you are part of a team that delivers quality, builds relationships, and moves projects forward.

We’re looking for dedicated, talented individuals who deliver excellence, thrive in collaborative environments, and value both meaningful work and work-life balance. If this sounds like you, we’d like to hear from you.

Please note that the salary information shown below is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate experience and qualifications, as well as various market and business considerations.

US Pay Range: $35 USD - $50 USD

Full-time employees receive a well-rounded benefit package including access to our company-sponsored Medical (including an HSA High Deductible option), Dental, Vision, FSA, and Supplemental Life Insurance plans. We also offer 100% company-paid Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability coverage. Employees are eligible to participate in our company's 401(k) plan with up to a 4% match. Additionally, employees receive paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, and are able to participate in employee ownership options. MacKay pays for expenses associated with licensure as well as annual performance bonuses.

Employment requires passing a pre-employment background check and drug screen.

As a federal contractor, we participate in E-Verify and are proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer.

new_jobs.description:
Job Title:
Assistant Director of Environmental Services
Location:
Sussex County, Delaware
Salary:
$95,000 - $145,000
Position Overview:

A municipal environmental services department is seeking an experienced Assistant Director of Environmental Services to support the operation, maintenance, permitting, and regulatory compliance of water and wastewater treatment facilities. This leadership role combines technical expertise, staff supervision, operational oversight, regulatory coordination, budgeting, and capital project support. The position serves as a key resource in ensuring reliable utility operations, permit compliance, and effective management of environmental services programs throughout the county.
Key Responsibilities:

Supervise and schedule technical and non-technical staff, including performance management, employee development, and disciplinary actions.
Assist with the operation, maintenance, and regulatory compliance of water and wastewater treatment facilities and associated infrastructure.
Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies regarding permits, inspections, compliance issues, and reporting requirements.
Prepare and renew NPDES permits, Land Treatment System permits, Air Pollution Control permits, and related regulatory documentation.
Review monitoring reports, maintain compliance records, and assist in responding to permit violations and inspections.
Support asset management, GIS-based tracking programs, procurement activities, and work order management systems.
Assist with operational decision-making involving process controls, maintenance priorities, staffing, scheduling, and facility performance.
Participate in the planning, review, and coordination of water and wastewater facility expansion, design, and construction projects.
Assist with the development and administration of operating and capital budgets, including expenditure monitoring and forecasting.
Oversee compliance with safety regulations and environmental requirements related to industrial and hazardous material operations.
Represent the department at meetings with stakeholders, consultants, contractors, elected officials, and regulatory agencies.
Participate in emergency response activities and a 24-hour rotating on-call schedule as required.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related field.
Minimum of 7-8 years of experience in water and wastewater treatment operations, environmental services, or related infrastructure systems.
Strong technical knowledge of water and wastewater treatment processes, transmission systems, pump stations, sludge handling, and disposal practices.
Experience with environmental permitting and regulatory compliance, including NPDES permits and air permitting programs.
Supervisory experience, including planning, assigning, reviewing, and evaluating staff performance.
Knowledge of federal, state, and local regulations governing water and wastewater facilities.
Experience with municipal budgeting, operational planning, and capital project support.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with regulatory agencies, elected officials, staff, and the public.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and ESRI GIS platforms.
Ability to work in both office and field environments, including access to confined spaces as necessary.

Preferred Experience/Skills:

Level IV Wastewater Operator Certification.
Experience operating and maintaining SCADA systems and biological process modeling software.
Knowledge of odor control systems and air scrubbing technologies.
Experience working within a unionized workforce environment.
Familiarity with GIS-based asset management systems and utility infrastructure management.
Strong leadership, organizational, and customer service skills.

Experience supporting large-scale water and wastewater capital improvement projects.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Imagine Everything. Build the Future with Hexion.

At Hexion, we push boundaries, rethink possibilities, and create real impact.
We activate science to deliver progress—developing breakthrough solutions that strengthen industries, protect communities, and drive a more sustainable future.

This is where bold thinkers, problem-solvers, and innovators come together to shape what’s next.
Whether you're engineering advanced materials, transforming manufacturing technologies, or leading strategic innovation, your ideas and actions leave a lasting mark. We cultivate an inclusive culture of growth, collaboration, and accountability, ensuring every contribution propels us forward.

We don’t follow the status quo—we challenge it, disrupt it, and improve it. Every role at Hexion is part of something bigger.

We invest in innovation, sustainability, and continuous development—equipping you with the tools, training, and opportunities to excel. With an unwavering commitment to safety, partnership, belonging, and impact, we empower you to lead change and strengthen industries worldwide.

Your Future Starts Here.

If you’re ready to push limits, reimagine what’s possible, and create the extraordinary,
Hexion is where you belong.

Anything is possible when you imagine everything.

Position Overview

The Environmental Engineer is an individual contributor responsible for supporting safe, compliant, and environmentally responsible operations at Hexion's Springfield, Oregon facility. This role helps ensure the site meets applicable Lane County, Oregon, and federal environmental regulations while supporting day-to-day execution of environmental programs, permit requirements, regulatory reporting, and compliance activities.

This position directly contributes to environmental performance by providing technical guidance, maintaining compliance systems, supporting environmental evaluations for projects and process changes, and helping translate operational data into clear compliance actions. The role serves as a key environmental resource for Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, and Site Leadership and supports a strong culture of environmental stewardship, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Job Responsibilities

Support Environmental Compliance & Program Execution

Manage site environmental programs to support compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements
Support day-to-day environmental compliance activities, including monitoring, inspections, recordkeeping, reporting, and corrective action follow-up
Maintain compliance with key environmental programs, including air, waste management, wastewater, stormwater, EPCRA, and SPCC requirements
Track environmental permit requirements and regulatory obligations to ensure site-specific compliance actions are completed on time

Provide Environmental Technical Guidance

Serve as a technical resource to Site Leadership, Operations, Maintenance, and Engineering teams
Provide guidance on permit conditions, environmental requirements, regulatory changes, and site best practices
Translate process, operational, and environmental data into usable compliance information
Support environmental awareness and understanding of site environmental expectations

Support Project, Process Change & Regulatory Authorization Activities

Evaluate projects, process changes, and operational modifications for environmental applicability
Identify environmental permitting or authorization needs related to site changes
Support preparation and submission of required environmental applications, reports, and regulatory documentation
Partner with internal stakeholders to ensure environmental requirements are incorporated into project planning and execution

Manage Reporting, Data & Compliance Tools

Support data collection, analysis, and submittal of required environmental reports, including Fire Marshal, Tier II, TRI, and other required regulatory reports
Develop, maintain, and improve spreadsheets, trackers, and compliance tools to support environmental program execution
Analyze compliance data to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement
Maintain organized environmental records and documentation to support audit readiness

Support Audits, Inspections & Continuous Improvement

Participate in internal audits, external audits, and regulatory agency inspections as needed
Support timely response to audit findings, agency requests, and corrective actions
Help identify practical improvements to strengthen compliance systems and streamline environmental work processes
Support continuous improvement initiatives that improve environmental performance, accountability, and operational efficiency

Minimum Qualifications

Required Qualifications

3 to 6 years of experience as an environmental engineer or environmental professional in a manufacturing, industrial, or regulated facility environment
Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related engineering field
Working knowledge of LRAPA, Oregon DEQ, and federal environmental regulations across multiple media
Strong working knowledge of air compliance and permitting requirements
Practical experience with wastewater permitting and compliance
Familiarity with waste management, stormwater, EPCRA, SPCC, and environmental reporting requirements
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and operate independently at times
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
Ability to influence without direct authority and work effectively across functions
Proficiency with spreadsheet tools, data tracking, and compliance management systems

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting environmental compliance in a chemical manufacturing environment
Experience preparing or supporting Tier II, TRI, emissions, wastewater, stormwater, or other regulatory reporting
Experience participating in regulatory inspections, audits, or agency interactions
SAP experience or experience with similar enterprise systems
Experience supporting environmental reviews for capital projects, process changes, or management of change activities

Travel Requirements

10% travel

Other

We are an Equal Opportunity, Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, pregnancy, race, national origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran or military status, status as a qualified individual with a disability or any other characteristic protected by law.

To be considered for this position candidates are required to submit an application for employment through our career site and, be at least 18 years of age. Any offer of employment will be conditioned upon successful completion of a drug test and background investigation, as well as authorization for the Company to conduct additional periodic background checks as required by the Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards (CFATS) or regulations adopted by the department of Homeland Security or other regulatory agencies. A prior criminal record is not an automatic bar to employment, and the Company will conduct an individualized assessment and reassessment, consistent with applicable law, prior to making any final employment decision.

new_jobs.title: Senior Sustainability Analyst - Environmental Compliance & Analytics
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Senior Analyst is responsible for supporting environmental data management, analytics, and regulatory compliance activities. This role supports the collection, validation, and reporting of environmental data across energy, waste, and environmental compliance programs; ensuring accuracy and consistency across systems and reporting processes. The Senior Analyst also supports renewable energy tracking and analysis, including maintaining program data, preparing reporting, and assisting with performance monitoring.

A Day In The Life

Sustainability Data Analytics:

Review Scope 1 and Scope 2 environmental datasets, including data validation, reconciliation, and discrepancy resolution.
Update and maintain energy and waste data tracking models to support ongoing performance monitoring and reporting.
Analyze data trends and anomalies in energy and waste performance and prepare summaries to support internal reporting and decision-making.
Collaborate with Internal Audit and cross-functional teams to enhance environmental data controls and processes.
Support the development and maintenance of forecasting models for energy and waste data, including updating inputs and assisting with output analysis.
Coordinate with Energy Engineering and internal teams to develop and implement project planning based on environmental analytics findings, including opportunity identification, resolution tracking progress, and resulting savings models and validation.

Renewable Energy Analytics & Program Execution:

Maintain renewable energy tracking tools and monitor progress toward renewable energy goals.
Compile and track renewable energy credits (RECs) from multiple sources.
Monitors and manage active solar arrays to ensure optimal performance. This includes energy production trending, and initiating repairs and maintenance for owned solar.
Support improvements to renewable energy data tracking and reporting processes.
Coordinate with internal teams, landlords, and vendors to support renewable energy projects and initiatives.
Monitor renewable project performance and coordinate issue resolution with internal stakeholders and vendors.
Support internal partners on landlord owned and operated onsite solar, including re-roofs, RTU replacements, and solar system repairs needed.

Environmental Compliance Support:

Maintain sustainability documentation and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support compliance with environmental regulations.
Support audit readiness activities, including documentation, data validation, and record organization.
Coordinate data and documentation required for sustainability disclosures.
Assist Sustainability team in preparation of data sets and reporting for various federal, state and local environmental compliance programs.
Assist in identifying and addressing gaps in data controls and compliance processes.

You'll Come With

Bachelor’s degree; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
3–5 years of experience in sustainability, environmental analytics, or related field.
Experience manipulating large data sets, collaboration with team members to provide suggestions on data management, provide data validation and auditing, reviewing current state of data-driven processes, development of KPI/dashboard, and work both independently and as part of team environment.
Advanced proficiency in data analytics tools such as: Excel, MS Access, Power BI or equivalent technologies.
Experience using reporting, visualizations, and analytical tools to build insights, communicate findings, and deliver actionable business solutions to stakeholders.
Able to connect various requirements into one synchronized process and work with various stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communications skills that reflect an ability to clarify complex issues.
Ability to work independently, collaboratively, and manage multiple competing projects to timely completion.

You will enjoy competitive wages, flexible hours, and an associate discount. Burlington’s benefits package includes medical, dental and vision coverage including life and disability insurance. new_jobs.title: Director of Operations | Geospatial Background | Pensacola, FL
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Director of Operations
to oversee the day-to-day operations and continued growth of a land surveying office in Pensacola, Florida.
This individual will take ownership of project delivery, scheduling, budgets, client relationships, staffing, and overall office performance. The ideal candidate has a strong background within the land surveying industry and has progressed beyond individual project management into broader operational and leadership responsibilities.
This is an opportunity for an experienced surveying professional to play a key role in the direction and growth of an established operation while maintaining strong relationships with both employees and clients.

Key Responsibilities

Oversee the daily operations
of the Pensacola surveying office.
Manage project schedules, workloads, deadlines, and resource allocation across multiple surveying teams.
Monitor project budgets, profitability, utilization, and overall financial performance
.
Work closely with Project Managers to ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget.
Maintain and grow relationships with existing clients
while supporting new business development.
Serve as a senior point of contact for key clients and help resolve project or contractual issues.
Oversee staffing needs, hiring, employee development, and team performance.
Coordinate field and office resources to maintain efficient project delivery.
Help establish and improve internal processes, workflows, and operational standards.
Review project pipelines and backlog to anticipate future staffing and resource needs.
Support proposals, scopes of work, fee development, and contract negotiations.
Partner with executive leadership on strategic planning and long-term growth
of the operation.
Foster a collaborative, accountable, and client-focused office culture.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience within land surveying, geomatics, or a closely related field
.
Previous experience managing multiple projects, teams, or an office/department
.
Strong understanding of project scheduling, budgets, utilization, and profitability.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing client relationships.
Strong leadership and people-management skills.
Experience overseeing both field and office surveying operations preferred.
Comfortable managing competing deadlines and allocating resources across multiple projects.
Experience with proposals, contracts, fee development, and business development is highly desirable.
Professional Surveyor and Mapper (PSM) license preferred
, but not necessarily required depending on operational and leadership experience.

Ideal Background

The ideal candidate is currently operating at the Operations Manager, Survey Manager, Department Manager, Regional Manager, Office Manager, or Director level
within a land surveying or civil engineering firm.
They should understand the technical side of surveying, but their primary strength should be running the business
: keeping teams busy, projects profitable, clients happy, schedules organized, and the office moving in the right direction.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer – Flight Automation & Drone Integrations
new_jobs.description:
At Airpelago, we are pioneering the inspection of power grids with drones. We combine modern drone technology, proprietary software, and expertise in drone regulations to help grid owners inspect and get insights about their assets, which our society is dependent on. As we continue to scale, we are looking for a Software Engineer to develop the flight automation software that makes our inspections autonomous, and to bring new drone platforms and payloads into our system.

Your mission

You will build and improve the software that plans, executes and monitors autonomous inspection flights. You will also develop integrations with new drone platforms and payloads, from evaluating an SDK to having the aircraft fly a full mission with our software in the field. You will work close to the hardware, close to the data, and close to the people who operate the system in production.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain our flight automation software, from mission planning to in-flight execution.
Integrate new drone platforms, flight controllers, and payloads (cameras, LiDAR, sensors) into our system.
Work with manufacturer SDKs and APIs, and evaluate new hardware for technical fit.
Build the tooling and abstractions that let us support several drone platforms without duplicating work.
Test and validate your work in the field, together with our operations and testing engineers.
Debug issues that cross the software/hardware boundary: logs, telemetry, radio links, and sensors.
Contribute to technical decisions on architecture, safety and reliability of autonomous flight.
Take ownership of your domain end to end, from idea to production.

What We're Looking For

At least 3 years of software development experience.
Experience integrating hardware and software - drones, cameras, sensors, embedded systems or robotics is a strong advantage.
Comfort working with SDKs, APIs and vendor documentation of varying quality.
Interest in getting out of the office: this role includes field testing with real aircraft.
Structured approach to testing and safety in systems where failures have physical consequences.
Ability to work autonomously and take ownership of a technical domain.
Full proficiency in Swedish and English, both written and verbal.
A valid B driver’s license, with comfort working outdoors and travelling for field testing.
Experience with camera geometry is a strong plus: projection models, calibration (intrinsics/extrinsics), and coordinate transformations.

Experience with MAVLink and DJI SDKs is beneficial but not a requirement. Curiosity and the ability to learn a new platform quickly matter more to us!

Why join Airpelago?

You will play a central role in transforming an industry with automated aerial data. We are currently on an exciting growth journey, and you will become part of a driven, passionate, and highly skilled team. We believe in achieving great things while having fun along the way - including an annual winter office abroad and recurring company gatherings. We offer a dynamic, high-trust environment where our technical innovations directly impact real-world operations and commercial success.
